How to put a logo in the middle of a QR code

No design software needed.

  1. Enter the link the code should open in the field above.
  2. Turn on Center Logo and upload a square PNG or JPG. A logo with a solid or white background works best.
  3. Choose a QR color and style. Dark on light is the safest for scanning.
  4. Download the PNG for screens and documents, or the SVG for print.
  5. Test with two phones before you use it.

How can a QR code still scan with a logo covering the middle?

QR codes include built-in error correction, extra data that lets a scanner rebuild information hidden by a smudge, tear or logo. A higher correction level can survive more covered area, but it also makes the pattern denser.

When you turn on a logo here, the tool raises the error correction level automatically so the code keeps enough redundancy. Even so, there is a limit. A small logo scans reliably, and a big logo can make it fail.

Logo size and scan reliability

These are practical guidelines, not guarantees. Always test the final file.

Logo sizeWhat to expect
Small (well under a fifth of the code's width)Scans reliably in most cases
Medium (around a fifth)Usually fine on a clean print, riskier on screens or worn surfaces
LargeHigh chance of scan failures, especially on older phones

Tips for a branded QR code that works

Branding should not cost you scans.

  • Keep the logo small and centered. Simple shapes beat detailed ones.
  • Keep strong contrast between the code and the background. Avoid light-on-dark inversions and pale brand colors.
  • Use a shorter link when you can, because a shorter link produces a simpler, easier-to-scan pattern.
  • Leave a blank margin around the code so scanners can find its edges.
  • Test on the real material, such as the printed flyer, the shop board or the packaging, not just the screen.
Where to Use It

Where a branded QR code works well

Packaging & labels

Give products a scannable, on-brand link to reviews, warranty or reorders.

Shop boards & standees

A recognizable logo in the code makes it look trustworthy.

Business cards & brochures

Link to your site or catalogue with a code that matches your identity.

Restaurant menus

Put the logo in the middle of a menu code for table tents and windows.

Events & posters

Branded codes look better on banners and invitations.

Social & digital ads

Use a PNG with your logo on flyers shared over messaging apps.
